answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The fable multiplier is published, charged in walnut, and vertex lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1228 identities would post 2382 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
